subject: Sizing request: reserved compute allotment and pricing sensitivity for Veridian
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@veridian.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask: reserved compute for Veridian platform expansion

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this. We are finalizing procurement planning for our next product cycle and are evaluating reserved compute options for a production rollout. High-level ask: pricing and guardrails for a reserved compute allotment that supports our mid-2027 ramp.

Quick context:
- Current POC uses mixed A100/T4 inference fleet; projected steady-state (by Q2 2027) ~50M generation tokens/day across inference and batch pipelines.
- Expected baseline sustained need: ~40 GPU-equivalents (A40/A100 mix) with a 10% burst headroom.
- Ideal commercial construct: 12/24/36 month reserve options with clear discount tiers and an indexed clause if GPU market prices spike/fall.

Questions we need answered to move forward:
1) What are your recommended baseline sizing packages (GPU-equivalents) for 12/24/36 month tenors?
2) Discount bands you typically offer at each tenor and at what commit sizes they trigger.
3) Mechanism for protecting customer vs provider on sudden GPU cost inflation (indexation, pass-through, or cap).
4) Any minimum commitment or exit penalties to be aware of for a Tier-1 enterprise buyer (we do not want surprise clawbacks).

Can we schedule a 30-min call this week to run through scenarios? Ideally include finance and product ops.

Thanks,
Alex Carter
VP, Infrastructure
Veridian.ai

[Attachment: veridian_requirements_summary.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Cc: Maya Sharma <maya@veridian.ai>

Alex — appreciate the concise brief. Happy to run scenarios. Proposed next steps:

- Quick 30-min sync to align on traffic shape (burst windows, seq lengths, peak concurrency). Can you do Thu 09/16 at 10:00 PT?
- I attached a small preliminary sizing template (veridian_prelim_sizing.xlsx) — if you can populate the 7-day peak profile and expected growth rate we’ll run three committed scenarios.
- We’ll model three tenors (12/24/36 months) and produce: committed GPU equivalents, expected monthly throughput, discount tier, and a proposed GPU-price-index clause for downside protection.

Preliminary notes (ballpark, subject to follow-up):
- If sustained baseline is ~40 GPU-eq, typical breakpoints we consider: 25–35 (small enterprise), 36–55 (mid), 56+ (strategic).
- Discount ranges (indicative): 10–20% for 12m, 18–30% for 24m, 28–42% for 36m depending on committed quantity and invoice cadence.

I’ve tentatively scheduled internal ops and finance for the call — can add legal if you want contract-level discussion.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: veridian_prelim_sizing.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sizing ask: reserved compute for Veridian — proposal scenarios + ask

Karthik / Neha — forwarding Veridian’s request (below). Quick internal ask: I drafted three commercial scenarios based on their stated baseline (~40 GPU-eq sustained). Please review and advise approval path / risks.

DRAFT scenarios (sizing + commercial):
- Scenario A — 12 month commit
  - Commit: 30 GPU-eq sustained
  - Allowance: +10% burst monthly
  - Indicative discount: 12% off list
  - Upside: Low entry friction; limited price protection clause (cap on pass-through)

- Scenario B — 24 month commit (recommended default)
  - Commit: 40 GPU-eq sustained
  - Allowance: +15% burst monthly
  - Indicative discount: 25% off list
  - Upside: Better unit economics; propose automatic capacity rebalancing every quarter

- Scenario C — 36 month strategic commit
  - Commit: 55 GPU-eq sustained
  - Allowance: +20% burst monthly
  - Indicative discount: 38% off list
  - Upside: deepest discount, longer-term price certainty; requires exec approval for discount exceedance >35%

Pricing sensitivity and protection: proposed "GPU Price Index" clause — if underlying spot market GPU unit cost moves >15% month-over-month for two consecutive months, either party may request a good-faith pricing adjustment (indexation window + cap). We need your guidance on acceptable thresholds and whether to include a floor.

Commercial asks from Sales/Ops:
- Fast-track approval to offer Scenario B as the standard commercial play (internal pre-approval to commit up to 45 GPU-eq for field motions).
- Authorization to offer up to 30% discount without exec sign-off; discounts >30% require pricing committee.
- For >50 GPU-eq requests, require Legal + Finance sign-off and a special SLA addendum (availability and warm-standby commitments).

Attachments (for modeling): veridian_proposal_draft_v1.pdf // gpu_pricing_sensitivity_model.csv

Can you reply with: (A) comfort with Scenario B pre-approval and (B) suggested edit to price-index thresholds and discount guardrails?

— Mateo

Thanks for the concise scenarios, Mateo. High level response and firm lines for field: 

1) Approvals
- I sign off on using Scenario B as the standard outbound offer for this engagement (24m / 40 GPU-eq). Sales can commit up to 45 GPU-eq under this pre-approval. Anything above that moves to pricing committee.
- We will cap pre-approved discounts at 30% (no exec needed). Discounts >30% and up to 38% require VP approval; >38% requires CFO/CEO approval.

2) Price protection clause
- Acceptable structure: implement a GPU Price Index with a symmetric band: if index moves +/-15% month-over-month for two consecutive months, trigger a review. Include a floor (no lower pass-through below -10%) to ensure predictability for both sides.
- For upside (customer protection vs price increases), propose a cap on pass-through of +20% for any single quarter and require finance-led reconciliation.

3) SLAs and operational requirements
- For commitments >=50 GPU-eq we require an SLA addendum (15 min P95 cold-start target for critical routes, availability target 99.5% monthly). Also require warm-standby provisions and a clause for capacity rebalancing windows.

4) Commercial concession
- I am comfortable authorizing a one-time $100k platform credit for ramp months (applied over first 3 invoices) to help close the sale, subject to deal registration and execution of the 24m contract. Finance (Neha) please confirm accounting treatment and runway.

Next steps: Neha, can you run the sensitivity model (attached) with the floor/cap thresholds above and confirm margin impact at 25% / 30% / 38% discount levels? If margins hold at 30% we approve; if not, we escalate to Pricing Committee (PC-9845).

Karthik
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
